name: git_log
description: Read-only commit history — what changed, when, and why it was described that way. The tool for understanding how a file or the whole tree got to its current state, without inferring intent from the diff alone.

cwd.description: Directory to run the log from, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside a git repository.

path.description: Limit history to commits touching this file or directory, relative to the workspace root. Omit for the whole repository's history.

max_entries.description: Upper bound on commits returned, newest first. A history longer than this is truncated and `truncated` is set.

message.description: First line of the commit message. Not the full body.

truncated.description: True if `max_entries` cut the history short of the full log.

errors.description: `cwd` does not resolve inside a git repository.
`cwd` or `path` resolves outside the workspace root and was refused before any git command ran.
The repository has no commits yet — a real, unremarkable state for a workspace just created.

safety_notes: Read-only. Commit messages are reported verbatim and never rewritten, summarized, or interpreted for tone — a message is evidence of what the author said at the time, and paraphrasing it here would be exactly the kind of hindsight relabeling `core/learning_protocol.md` forbids for this repository's own decision records.
